edges.description: Reduced receptor number/affinity impairs signalling in insulin target cells.
The insulin receptor is expressed in the kidney; biallelic INSR loss produces a renal phenotype (hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis) independent of the diabetic state.
Blunted receptor signalling produces the defining extreme insulin-resistant state.
Target tissues require supraphysiologic insulin, driving compensatory hypersecretion.
Residual insulin action plus massive hyperinsulinaemia yields fluctuating glucose.
Fasting hypoglycaemia from severely increased insulin levels early in life.
Postprandial hyperglycaemia from failure of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal.
High insulin stimulates keratinocyte IGF receptors.
Hyperinsulinaemia drives ovarian hyperandrogenism in females.
Chronic hyperstimulation leads to eventual secretory failure.
High insulin may interact with IGF-I receptors and feedback-reduce GH secretion.

nodes.description: Biallelic pathogenic variants in the insulin receptor gene (INSR, 19p13.2) reduce the number and/or function of cell-surface insulin receptors, most commonly through missense substitutions that impair receptor processing, insulin-binding affinity, or tyrosine-kinase activity. This is the initiating molecular lesion of the syndrome.

evidence.reference_title: Genealogical Rabson-Mendenhall syndrome caused by INSR gene mutation.
evidence.snippet: The novel mutation c.3670G>A in exon 21, inherited from the father, is likely to impair insulin receptor function by disrupting tyrosine kinase activity

evidence.reference_title: Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome: Analysis of the Clinical Characteristics and Gene Mutations in 42 Patients.
evidence.snippet: The mutation also caused a reduction in the affinity of the receptor to insulin

nodes.description: Pancreatic beta-cell hypersecretion produces the extreme hyperinsulinaemia that is the earliest biochemical hallmark of the syndrome (median fasting insulin ~300 uIU/mL, versus a normal range of 5-20 uIU/mL). Chronic hyperinsulinaemia cross-activates IGF-1 receptors in skin and ovary and ultimately exhausts beta-cell reserve.

evidence.reference_title: Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome: Analysis of the Clinical Characteristics and Gene Mutations in 42 Patients.

evidence.reference_title: Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome: Analysis of the Clinical Characteristics and Gene Mutations in 42 Patients.

nodes.description: Recurrent diabetic ketoacidosis emerges in the second decade as insulin secretion declines and is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality.

nodes.description: Loss of functional insulin receptor blunts the downstream insulin receptor signalling pathway, principally the PI3K-AKT metabolic arm, in liver, skeletal muscle, and adipose tissue, so target tissues fail to mount a normal glucose-lowering response to insulin.

evidence.reference_title: Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome: Analysis of the Clinical Characteristics and Gene Mutations in 42 Patients.

nodes.description: Insulin sensitizers are first-line to lower glucose and HbA1c, though their effect diminishes over time and often requires dose escalation and multidrug therapy. Pioglitazone has normalized blood glucose in a reported case.

evidence.reference_title: INSR-Related Severe Insulin Resistance Syndrome.
evidence.snippet: Insulin sensitizers are used first to decrease levels of glucose and glycosylated hemoglobin (HbA1c); however, their effect diminishes with time, often requiring dose adjustments and multidrug therapy.

nodes.description: Overt insulin-resistant diabetes mellitus develops as beta-cell reserve fails; reported in about 76% of evaluable pooled cases, all diagnosed before age 23 (mean 9.4 years).

evidence.reference_title: Rabson-Mendenhall Syndrome: Analysis of the Clinical Characteristics and Gene Mutations in 42 Patients.
evidence.snippet: Diabetes was reported in 25 cases (25/33, 75.76%) all of which were diagnosed before 23 years old.

nodes.description: Recombinant leptin (metreleptin), used off-label, lowers HbA1c over long-term follow-up, likely through appetite suppression and reduced BMI rather than direct restoration of insulin signalling; lower BMI may worsen growth-hormone resistance.

nodes.description: Nephrocalcinosis with hypercalciuria is an almost invariable renal feature, apparently tissue-autonomous to renal INSR loss rather than secondary to hyperglycaemia.

nodes.description: Recombinant human IGF-1 signals through the IGF-1 receptor, partially bypassing the defective insulin receptor. It improves glycaemic control and fasting tolerance in early life with some growth enhancement, but benefits are limited and it does not prevent decompensation to diabetes; continuous subcutaneous infusion may outperform bolus injection.

nodes.description: The insulin receptor is expressed throughout the nephron. Biallelic INSR loss produces hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis that appear tissue-autonomous (present with normotension and stable glomerular function), rather than being a secondary complication of hyperglycaemia.
